column3: Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew uses the fear verb for the sanctuary; BSB says “have reverence.”
The Hebrew says to “walk” in the statutes, “keep” the commandments, and “do them”; BSB says “follow” and “carefully keep.”
The Hebrew repeats the giving verb for rains, the land’s produce, and the tree’s fruit, with singular collective “tree”; BSB uses “give,” “yield,” and “bear,” and plural “trees.”
The Hebrew says to eat “your bread to satisfaction”; BSB broadens this to “have your fill of food to eat.”

The Hebrew says they were slaves “to them,” without repeating the Egyptians’ name; BSB identifies the masters as “the Egyptians.”
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew makes “your soul” the subject of abhorring the judgments; BSB simply addresses “you” as despising the ordinances.
The Hebrew says the diseases consume “eyes”; BSB uses the abstract “sight.”
The Hebrew says they will be defeated “before” their enemies; BSB specifies defeat “by” their enemies.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew names “the pride of your strength”; BSB says “your stubborn pride.”
The Hebrew uses singular collective “the tree of the land”; BSB uses plural “the trees.”
The Hebrew speaks of adding “a blow” sevenfold; BSB says “multiply your plagues.”
The Hebrew calls the animals “the beast of the field”; BSB uses “wild animals.”
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew repeats “I also” and the walking image; BSB states “I” with each action but says “act with hostility” for the first.
The Hebrew says “you shall gather into your cities” joined by “and”; BSB interprets this as “Though you withdraw into your cities.”
The Hebrew uses the image of breaking “the staff of bread”; BSB says cutting off “your supply of bread.”
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew retains both “wrath” and “contrariness” in the walking clause; BSB says “walk in fury against you.”
The Hebrew repeats “you shall eat” and “flesh” separately for sons and daughters; BSB combines them into one clause.
The Hebrew repeats “corpses” for the people and their idols; BSB varies the words as “lifeless bodies” and “lifeless remains.”
